_readme: Editable source of truth for BC freshwater fishing-regulation POINT CURATION. One entry per distinct (regulation, locator string), grouped by the split anchor kind it maps to in stream_sections/splits.json. To curate a row: fill `target` and/or `coord`/`split_id`, optionally set `label`, move any research into `notes`, then set `status` to "curated". Converted 1:1 from 17-locators-to-curate.md; see that file for the how-to.

_schema.id: stable unique slug (kebab of name + short content hash)
_schema.name_verbatim: regulation title exactly as it appears in the md (may be truncated)
_schema.src: where the locator came from: name | entry | rule | except
_schema.locator_text: the locator string to resolve to a point/reach (may be truncated in the source md)
_schema.anchor_kind: split anchor.type this locator maps to; see anchor_kinds
_schema.status: todo | curated | manual | not_applicable | auto | deferred (default 'todo'; 'auto' = resolved for free by the combine-phase lake split per docs/04, no authored split needed; 'deferred' = looked at but unsolved, sorts last)
_schema.target: resolved feature target: object like {blk:..} / {wsc:..} / {gnis:..}, or '' if unset
_schema.coord: [lon, lat] once a single point is chosen, else null
_schema.label: short human label for the point/section, or ''
_schema.notes: free text; carries any human research/annotation verbatim
_schema.full_regulation: the COMPLETE regulation block (all rules) for this water/MU from the synopsis, for human context; '' if unmatched
_schema.resolver_hint: how to FIND the point (falls_obstacle/dam_weir_fence/...); see resolver_hints
_schema.entry_id: stable id of the source reg entry (waterbody+MU+reg); groups rows that share one synopsis listing. See oneoff/waterbody_splits.py + docs/18.

anchor_kinds.point: split anchor.type=point (coord cut perpendicular to the mainstem)
anchor_kinds.confluence: split anchor.type=confluence (cut at a tributary mouth, keyed on tributary_wsc)
anchor_kinds.lake: split anchor.type=lake (lake polygon boundary; often already splits the BLK)
anchor_kinds.area_boundary: split anchor.type=area_boundary (polygon boundary, e.g. a park)
anchor_kinds.mu_boundary: split anchor.type=mu_boundary (shared line between two MUs)
anchor_kinds.lake_io: NEW lake_io op (immediate lake_inlets union lake_outlets) — not yet built
anchor_kinds.buffer: NEW buffer op (point + radius) — not yet built
anchor_kinds.not_a_split: NOT a curated split: whole-water / tributary-SET / EXCEPT-exclusion / map-only
anchor_kinds.unclassified: reach whose split type is not yet decided — pick one during curation

locators.locator_text: in Skeena River Section 4
locators.full_regulation:
There are two separate Class II waters on the Skeena River (non-residents and non-resident aliens require separate licences describing
which section they are fishing): (a) from Exchamsiks River to 1.5 km upstream of Kitsumkalum River (known as "Skeena River 2"), July 1-Sept 30; and (b) 1.5 km upstream of Zymoetz River (known as "Skeena River Section 4"), July 1-Dec 31; Steelhead Stamp not mandatory for
Skeena River 2 unless fishing for steelhead. Steelhead Stamp is mandatory in Skeena River Section 4 during the Classified Waters period
from July 1-Dec 31
Angling prohibited for non-guided non-resident aliens in Skeena River Section 4 on Saturdays and Sundays in two zones: (a) Shegunia
River confluence to Sedan Creek confluence July 1-Dec 31 (See map page 54), and (b) Chimdemash Creek confluence to 1.5 km upstream of
Zymoetz River confluence, July 1 - Dec 31, (See map page 55)
